latest_release.body:
# QuestDB 10.2.0

QuestDB 10.2.0 adds `GROUPING SETS`, `ROLLUP` and `CUBE`, row-level retention for materialized views, a `DEDUP SKIP` mode that keeps the first-written row, and opt-in power-loss durability for WAL tables, enabled with `cairo.commit.mode=adaptive`. QWP ingestion of small messages is much faster, and this release fixes a large batch of wrong-result, crash and hang bugs in queries, out-of-order ingestion and Parquet partitions.

This release contains **a few breaking changes**. Read the [Breaking changes](#breaking-changes-boom) section before you upgrade, especially if you create materialized views with `LIMIT` or window functions, send the designated timestamp twice over QWP, or may need to downgrade after using `DEDUP SKIP`.

For any questions or feedback, please join us on [Slack](https://slack.questdb.com/) or on [Discourse](https://community.questdb.com/).

See also our _prettier_ [release notes](https://questdb.com/release-notes/) page.

## Breaking changes :boom:

- **`CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` rejects `LIMIT` in queries that read the base table, and base-table window functions nested in expressions or `SAMPLE BY` subqueries.** Replaying older `SHOW CREATE` output that contains them fails. [#7263](https://github.com/questdb/questdb/pull/7263)
- **QWP rejects table blocks that carry the designated timestamp twice**, once through `at(...)` and once as a named column. Before this change, QuestDB accepted them and stored wrong timestamps. A sender that uses both forms on one table now gets a schema error on every later batch for that table. [#8052](https://github.com/questdb/questdb/pull/8052)
- **An unknown `cairo.commit.mode` value now fails startup**, instead of silently selecting `nosync`. [#7411](https://github.com/questdb/questdb/pull/7411)
- **After 10.2.0 has run on a database, downgrading, writing with the older version and upgrading again is not supported.** See [downgrade to an earlier release](https://questdb.com/docs/concepts/durability/#downgrade). [#7411](https://github.com/questdb/questdb/pull/7411)
- **Downgrading after using `DEDUP SKIP`:** older versions treat `SKIP` tables as `UPSERT` without an error, and suspend WAL apply when they replay a logged `ALTER TABLE ... DEDUP SKIP`. [#7885](https://github.com/questdb/questdb/pull/7885)

## Highlights

### `GROUPING SETS`, `ROLLUP` and `CUBE`

`GROUP BY` and `SAMPLE BY` now accept `ROLLUP`, `CUBE` and `GROUPING SETS`, with the `GROUPING()` and `GROUPING_ID()` functions. One query returns subtotals and a grand total in a single scan of the input:

```sql
SELECT symbol, side, sum(amount)
FROM trades
GROUP BY ROLLUP(symbol, side);
```

Grouping sets run in parallel where the plan allows. `SAMPLE BY` grouping sets support `FILL` with `NULL`, constants or `NONE`. `cairo.sql.max.grouping.sets` caps how many grouping sets one query expands to (default 4096). Grouping sets do not vectorize: they ran 1.4x slower than the equivalent `UNION ALL` of plain `GROUP BY`s serially, and up to 6.9x slower in parallel, in the PR's benchmark. [#6853](https://github.com/questdb/questdb/pull/6853)

### Passthrough views and row-level retention

Materialized views can now be passthrough views: a filtered copy of a table (`SELECT ... WHERE`, no `SAMPLE BY`), kept up to date as rows arrive. The new `EXPIRE ROWS` policy adds row-level retention on top, and hides expired rows of a materialized view from every query: `WHEN <predicate>`, `KEEP LATEST`, `KEEP [N] HIGHEST|LOWEST`, or a window predicate. For monotonic `WHEN` policies, such as `ts < now()`, a background job also frees the disk; `cairo.mat.view.row.expiry.cleanup.*` settings control it. `ALTER MATERIALIZED VIEW ... SET EXPIRE ROWS` and `... DROP EXPIRE` change a view's policy. [#7263](https://github.com/questdb/questdb/pull/7263)
